reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses strengthening mechanisms in Co-rich TRIP-HEAs, phase formation rules in HfMoNbTaW, and heterogeneous deformation, but none addresses the effect of V substitution on electronegativity, bonding heterogeneity, dislocation motion, or plasticity in NbZrTiHfMo. The key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Reducing Mo content and adding V lowers electronegativity mismatch and bonding heterogeneity in BCC refractory HEAs
Lower bonding heterogeneity eases dislocation motion and improves room-temperature plasticity
V provides sufficient solution strengthening to maintain high yield strength near 1719 MPa
Partial Mo substitution by V (20–30%) retains a single-phase disordered BCC structure
